Children's stories come to life.|Baylan Skoll|}} '''Peridea''' was an [[extragalactic]] [[planet]] located in the [[far galaxy]]. It was the [[homeworld]] of the [[Noti]] and once the center of the [[Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri]], which eventually collapsed. [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] and [[Bokken Jedi]] [[Ezra Bridger]] were [[Exile (punishment)|banished]] to Peridea from the known [[The galaxy|galaxy]] by a pod of [[purrgil]] following the [[Liberation of Lothal]], on Bridger's request. The [[Arcana Star Map]] of the [[Nightsisters|Witches of Dathomir]] depicted a [[Pathway to Peridea]] from the main galaxy. According to [[Baylan Skoll]], [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi Younglings]] shared tales of Peridea throughout their childhood. The [[Planetary ring|rings]] of the planet consisted of [[purrgil]] [[bone]]s, as members of the species came to Peridea to die. ==Description== {{Quote|Be warned. Nomads wander this wasteland and prey upon each other for survival.|Enoch, to Sabine Wren|}} Peridea was a [[planet]] located in the distant [[far galaxy]], far away from [[the galaxy|the one]] presided over by the [[New Republic]]. The planetary surface, barren from war, was occupied by vast wastelands including grasslands, plains, [[Lake (disambiguation)|lakes]], and meadows, while its [[atmosphere]] was breathable to [[human]]s, [[Chiss]], [[Togruta]], and [[Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak]]s. It had a massive [[Planetary ring|ring]] made up of the [[bone]]s of [[purrgil]] surrounding it, as the creatures came to the planet to [[Death|die]]. [[File:Peridea_graveyard_ring.png|left|thumb|240x240px|The planetary ring around Peridea was comprised of the bones of dead purrgil]] Peridea was the [[homeworld]] of the [[Noti]] [[species]], who moved around in mobile settlements to avoid the dangers, and the wastes were populated by [[Howler]]s as well as a [[Unidentified reptavian (Peridea)|species of small reptavian]] native to the planet. There were also roaming [[Bandits of Peridea|groups of bandits]] who preyed on the lonesome stragglers who had ventured off onto the surface. A significant portion of the planet's culture revolved around the ancient [[Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri]]. Several towering statues depicting those who originally populated the planet dotted the landscape. Around [[9 ABY]], three [[witch]]es calling themselves the [[Great Mothers]] maintained a [[Great Mothers' Fortress|fortress]] which included above and underground [[henge]]s and contained vast catacombs. ==History== ===Myths and legends=== {{Quote|Do you miss it? The Order.''"
"''I miss... the idea of it. But not the truth, the weakness. There was no future there.''"
"''And you clearly see one here? In this wasteland?''"
"''I see what once was the great Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri. The existence of the Great Mothers confirms this.''"
"''They seem eager to leave this place. Maybe we should, too.''"
"''Perhaps they flee a power greater than their own. Something calls to me. Can't you hear it? Something stirs here. Can't you see it?|Shin Hati and Baylan Skoll|}} [[File:BaylanSkoll-FFA.png|thumb|320x320px|Baylan Skoll discovered the myths of Peridea's graveyards in the Jedi Archives]] Due to its [[extragalactic]] location, much that was known about Peridea to the inhabitants of the galaxy came from legends and tales. One such tale was the [[Pathway to Peridea]], popular among the [[Youngling]]s of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]] during the time when Baylan Skoll studied there. The tale of the Pathway described Peridea as a legendary planet outside of the main galaxy, which could be reached by following the Pathway starting from the planet [[Seatos]] on the [[Denab system]]. Skoll initially considered the stories to be mere children's tales,{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} however he eventually discovered the same legends on the [[Jedi Archives]]; there, Peridea was described as the end of the purrgils' last migration route, where they would go to pass away among their kind in a vast planetary "graveyard" ring. Another legend about Peridea existed among the [[Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir]]; it described the planet as the original home of their people, who rode the purrgil to travel between galaxies. A [[star map]] depicting the route from Seatos to Peridea was constructed at some point long before the [[New Republic Era]] and hidden in the [[Nightsisters' Temple]] on [[Arcana]]. By combining the map and the [[Seatos reflex point|reflex point]] on the henge temple on Seatos, a Witch could activate a [[holograph]]ic map which would give detailed instructions on how to reach Peridea, going as far as to provide usable [[hyperspace]] coordinates. ===Ancient history=== {{Quote|That is Peridea. The ancient home world of my ancestors, the Dathomiri.''"
"''The Jedi archives spoke of this place. It was the end of a migration route used by the star whales as they traversed the void from one galaxy to the other.''"
"''My people were the first to harness and ride the creatures in the days before time was counted.|Morgan Elsbeth and Baylan Skoll|}} At some point during its ancient history, a massive fortress was constructed on Peridea with an inscription that blessed the rule of the [[Zeffo]] [[Zeffo Sage|Sage]] [[Kujet]] and his reign. The inscription was written in the ancient [[Ur-Kittât]] script. At some point in time, Kujet's fortress came to be inhabited by the Dathomiri Nightsisters, with [[architect droid]] [[Huyang]] believing the planet to have become the center of their Witch Kingdom. Eventually, the fortress was abandoned by all but three witches, who came to call themselves the [[Great Mothers]]. They entered a long sleep at some time after this. During their hibernation, a [[Far galaxy war|war]] occurred in the far galaxy, which resulted in the galaxy and Peridea becoming largely dead and barren.{{HomeVideoCite|set=Ahsoka: The Complete First Season|featurette=Darkness Rising}} ===Imperial Era=== ====Exiled by the whales==== [[File:Purrgil_Ultra.jpg|thumb|220x220px|A purrgil Ultra carries the Chimaera away from Lothal|left]] During the [[Galactic Civil War]], [[Bokken Jedi]] [[Ezra Bridger]] joined the [[Phoenix Squadron]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and engaged in a long campaign to liberate his homeworld of [[Lothal]]. After encountering the purrgil in the [[Mining Guild]]'s [[Asteroid Belt Gas Refinery]] and establishing a [[Psychometry|psychometric]] connection with them through [[the Force]],{{Rebels|The Call}} Bridger eventually called for their assistance during the [[Liberation of Lothal]]{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} in [[1 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' During a pivotal battle against the occupation forces led by [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], the purrgil appeared out of hyperspace and destroyed his blockade above the planet. This allowed a pod led by a [[Purrgil Ultra]] to capture his flagship, the ''[[Chimaera]]'', and carry it whole along with Bridger and Thrawn in hyperspace. Heavily injured by the effort, the purrgil arrived at Peridea, leaving the two stranded with no way back. ====Survivors in a land of dreams==== While in exile for more than a [[Standard decade|decade]], the two eventually developed a close contact with the locals, using them to further their respective goals. Bridger escaped to the planet's wastelands and came close to the [[Noti]] nomads, learning their [[Noti language|language]] and living in a mobile home in one of their mobile encampments. He earned their trust by helping them repel the bandits that harassed them, and helped them develop defensive maneuvers to counter their attacks.{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}} He also deepened his connection with the Force during his stay on Peridea.{{InsiderCite|227|Born to Rebel}} Meanwhile, Thrawn discovered the Nightsister fortress and awoke its three inhabitants, the Nightsister Great Mothers, who discovered their way of life had been destroyed during the war that left the far galaxy dead and abandoned. Carefully creating a plan to return to the galaxy from the depths of Peridea,{{Twitter|username=StarWarsUK|url=status/1730889552955376043|name=''[[Star Wars]]'' UK|date=2023-12-02|quote=Thrawn carefully planned his return from the depths of Peridea. Discover his intentions on @DisneyPlusUK.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/AaWDZ}} Thrawn enlisted the Great Mothers' help in contacting one of his closest allies, fellow Nightsister [[Morgan Elsbeth]], through her [[dream]]s to ask for her help in locating him. In return, Thrawn would deliver the Great Mothers from Peridea and take with them their precious cargo. Thrawn would keep military structure on the planet, and would gather intel on the whereabouts of [[Ezra Bridger]]. His soldiers also took on the name of [[Night Trooper]]s.The Night Troopers would tame a [[Sabine Wren's howler|Howler]] during this time. ===New Republic Era=== ====Morgan Elsbeth's discovery==== [[File:Ct-05_on_the_eye_of_sion.png|thumb|240x240px|Morgan Elsbeth's forces constructed the ''Eye of Sion'' in secret over Seatos]] Following the end of the Civil War and the establishment of the [[New Republic]] in the place of the Galactic Empire, Morgan Elsbeth, having learned of Thrawn's fate by the Great Mothers' reaching out, began researching his possible whereabouts and actively working for his return. At some point around 9 ABY, her efforts caught the attention of former [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], who tracked her down to her hiding place in the village of [[Calodan]] on [[Corvus]] and, with the help of [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]] apprehended her{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 13: The Jedi}} to New Republic custody. Unbeknownst to Tano, [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|Elsbeth's forces]] had already concluded Thrawn's extragalactic location and began constructing a massive [[hyperspace transport ring]], the ''[[Eye of Sion]]'', to retrieve the Grand Admiral from his exile. With Elsbeth herself swiftly [[Attack on the Vesper|rescued from captivity]] by mercenaries Baylan Skoll and his apprentice [[Shin Hati]],{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}} and Hati taking possession of the Nightsister star map from Arcana, Elsbeth's [[Star Navigator droid]]s interpolated the coordinates to Peridea and, following a brief [[Incident on Seatos|skirmish]] with Tano{{Ahsoka|Part Four: Fallen Jedi}} successfully executed the jump through the [[intergalactic void]] to the legendary planet. Upon their arrival, they were greeted by the Great Mothers in the temple, and finally rendezvoused with Thrawn after his decades in exile. Meanwhile, Tano's Padawan [[Sabine Wren]], who had surrendered the star map to Skoll in exchange for passage to Peridea, discovered Bridger living as a nomad among the native Noti, and joined their clan. ====Friends and enemies reunited==== [[File:Eye_of_sion_holding_cell.png|thumb|240x240px|Sabine Wren arrived at Peridea as a prisoner|left]] Eventually Tano, determined to rescue Wren and put an end to Thrawn's threat before it could rise again arrived at the planet as well, carried in the mouth of a purrgil. Having been informed of her approach by the Great Mothers' magick, Thrawn had already ordered his [[Captain of the Guard]] [[Enoch]] to deploy an extensive field of [[space mine]]s around the planet, which detonated on the whales as soon as they arrived, severely injuring them and forcing them to abandon Tano and her ship. Hunted down by Elsbeth's [[RP82 Fiend fighter]]s, Ahsoka was forced to hide her shuttle in the graveyard ring, where she was attacked by the ''Eye of Sion''{{'s}} [[turbolaser]]s after once again being detected by the Mothers. With nowhere else to go, Tano was forced to ditch her ship and companion Huyang and land on the surface. There, she encountered Baylan Skoll, who had abandoned his Padawan in pursuit of a greater power he sensed hiding on the planet; the two briefly dueled but with both preoccupied in their own missions, the battle was cut short when Huyang bombed Skoll, giving Tano time to escape. On the meantime, Hati and a group of bandits had located the Noti clan Wren and Bridger were hiding with, and accompanied by two [[squad]]s of Night Troopers on board [[LAAT/le patrol gunship]]s had engaged the pair. Outnumbered, the two were soon encircled, but their execution was delayed when Ahsoka jumped into the battle, having arrived at the encampment just in time to witness her Padawan's peril. With most troopers killed in the skirmish, Thrawn ordered the survivors to return to the ''Chimaera'', leaving the two Jedi and Sabine alone to cheer their reunion. While Tano, Wren, and Bridger were preoccupied, Thrawn's forces completed the transfer of coffins from the crypt below the Great Mothers' Fortress onto the ''Chimaera''. Thrawn also dispatched a pair of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] to destroy the Jedi, who repelled the attack and stormed the Great Mothers' Fortress. Thrawn managed to delay the Jedi by deploying a contingent of Night Troopers who had been resurrected by Nightsister [[magick]]. Tano also defeated Elsbeth in combat. In an attempt to kill the Jedi and Wren, Thrawn ordered the ''Chimaera'' to destroy the fortress. The ''Chimaera'' managed to dock with the ''Eye of Sion'' and returned to the main galaxy, leaving Tano and Wren stranded on Peridea. Tano and Wren survived the bombardment and were rescued by [[Huyang]]. Despite Thrawn's efforts, Bridger managed to board the ''Chimaera'' and reunited with General [[Hera Syndulla]] in the main galaxy. Following Thrawn's escape Wren, Tano, and Huyang settled among the Noti. Meanwhile, Hati sought out the bandits while Skoll sought the mysterious source of power on Peridea that was seemingly connected to the powerful [[Force wielder]]s known as [[the Ones]]. ==Inhabitants== ===Natives=== {{Main|Noti}} {{Quote|They're peaceful people.|Ezra Bridger|}} [[File:Noti.png|thumb|312x312px|A Noti]] Peridea's native inhabitants were the Noti and the bandits. The Noti were a species of small [[Sentience|sentient]] nomads with rock-like shells on their backs they used for hiding. They lived in mobile [[Noti's Pod Mobile House|pod-shaped homes]] which they drove around the planet in tight-knit communities to avoid the surface's dangers and were known to be very peaceful, using only primitive weapons, such as [[slingshot]]s. The bandits were tall [[humanoid]]s who moved around in the backs of native [[howler]]s, forming hunting parties to attack Noti communities. They were armed with a variant of [[blaster rifle]]s and wore [[Color|red]] armor, with hunting party leaders also wearing large decorated helmets. ===Legendary inhabitants=== The Dathomiri were also said to have lived on the planet, with three powerful witches still residing in the fortress by 9 ABY and Huyang believing them to have made the planet a capital for their civilization, the Witch Kingdom of Dathomir. However, their way of life had been destroyed during the far galaxy war, and the Great Mothers desired to travel with Thrawn away from the now-barren Peridea. ===Immigrated species=== As a result of their forceful exile by the purrgil, a [[Thrawn's forces|detachment]] of [[human]] [[stormtrooper]]s calling themselves the [[Night Trooper]]s were forced to survive on the planet for nearly a decade, their numbers dwindling with each passing year. In addition, the Jedi and rebel fugitive [[Ezra Bridger]] settled among a Noti clan and became their leader. After being stranded on Peridea by Thrawn, the Jedi [[Ahsoka Tano]], the [[Mandalorian]] [[Sabine Wren]], and the [[architect droid]] [[Huyang]] settled among the Noti clan that Bridger had befriended. ==Behind the scenes== Peridea first appeared in the [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]'', released in [[2023]]. [[Timothy Zahn]] confirmed in an interview at the Dragon Con [[2018]] that where Grand Admiral Thrawn had been sent to by the purrgil after "[[Family Reunion – and Farewell]]," the series finale of ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', had already been decided.{{YouTube|channel=@StarWarsExplained|name=Star Wars Explained|video=GYUk_LmQKz4|text=Timothy Zahn Full Interview – Dragon Con 2018|date=2018-09-08}} Establishing shots of the landscape around the Great Mothers' Fortress on Peridea feature [[Wikipedia:Loch Sionascaig|Loch Sionascaig]], [[Wikipedia:Fionn Loch (Suilven)|Fionn Loch]], and neighboring lochs as well as the mountains [[Wikipedia:Suilven|Suilven]] and [[Wikipedia:Stac Pollaidh|Stac Pollaidh]] in [[Wikipedia:Scotland|Scotland's]] [[Wikipedia:Assynt|Assynt]]-[[Wikipedia:Coigach|Coigach]] National Scenic Area in the [[Wikipedia:Northwest Highlands|Northwest Highlands]].
